title: Blackbaud and Element451 Expand Connected Campus Ecosystem to Deliver More Connected, AI-Powered Experiences Across the Student Lifecycle
summary: Blackbaud and Element451 today announced a strategic partnership that enables AI-powered engagement and action across recruitment, admissions and student success and helps higher education institutions connect the technology, data and workflows supporting students throughout their journey.
body_markdown:
*Strategic partnership brings together connected institutional systems and agentic AI to give colleges and universities greater choice, reduce complexity and help teams better support students from prospect through lifelong engagement*


**Charleston, S.C. (Nov. 16, 2026)** — Blackbaud (NASDAQ: BLKB), the world’s leading provider of AI-powered solutions for social impact, and Element451, the AI platform that moves every student forward, today announced a strategic partnership that enables AI-powered engagement and action across recruitment, admissions and student success and helps higher education institutions connect the technology, data and workflows supporting students throughout their journey. This partnership advances Blackbaud’s Connected Campus, which brings together the systems, data and workflows institutions rely on so teams can work with greater visibility and less complexity.


Colleges and universities are navigating enrollment pressures, constrained resources and rising expectations to deliver more personalized experiences, often while relying on fragmented systems and lean teams. The Connected Campus is designed to address those challenges by connecting institutional systems and data so teams can operate with greater visibility, reduce complexity and direct more of their resources toward the people and priorities that matter most.


Through the partnership, Element451 brings its Bolt Agent Platform and Element AI CRM into the Connected Campus ecosystem, extending the vision into the areas of student recruitment, admissions, engagement and success. Together, Blackbaud and Element451 are focused on giving institutions greater choice in how they build their technology environment while creating stronger connections across the student lifecycle.


“Our customers want the power of the industry’s most modern, best-of-breed solutions in each area of their institution—and they want those solutions to work together to help them accomplish more,” said Mark Davis, vice president of education products at Blackbaud. “Our partnership with Element451 brings that vision to life through an innovative approach to AI that connects institutional insights with action. By bringing complementary strengths together across our Connected Campus ecosystem, we’re helping teams put AI to work, deliver more personalized student experiences and focus their expertise where it makes the greatest difference.”


Blackbaud’s Strategic Partnership with Student First brings together capabilities spanning student information, enrollment, financial aid, scholarships, advancement, finance and tuition payments. Element451 adds AI-powered engagement and action across recruitment, admissions and student success.


Together, these ecosystem relationships are designed to allow colleges and universities to adopt technology based on their institution’s individual needs and move toward a more connected environment at their own pace.


“Institutions have spent years buying solutions one at a time and then asking lean teams to make them work together,” said James Novak, Chief Executive Officer of Element451. “The Connected Campus changes that by designing the whole stack as one, and we’re proud to join Blackbaud, Student First, and Doctums in building it. Element451 brings the piece that reaches people. Our agents don’t wait to be asked. They spot the prospect who’s gone quiet and the student who’s falling behind, and they act, while staff keep the decisions that shape a student’s path.”


Element451’s Bolt AI agents can support outreach, follow-up and application-related workflows while allowing institutional staff to retain ownership of the decisions that shape a student’s path. Element AI CRM, which supports marketing and admissions, student success, and continuing education and workforce teams, is designed to:


- **Create more connected student experiences.** Connect technology and information supporting students from prospect and enrollment through student success, alumni engagement and advancement.
- **Turn connected data into meaningful action.** Use AI-powered agents and workflows to help teams follow up with prospects and students at scale while keeping people at the center of important decisions.
- **Reduce technology fragmentation.** Enable information to move more effectively between institutional systems so teams spend less time navigating disconnected tools and manual processes.
- **Increase choice and flexibility.** Allow institutions to select technology that meets their individual needs rather than requiring a single-system approach. Element451 can provide its AI CRM or deploy Bolt agents alongside CRMs institutions already use.
- **Improve visibility across campus.** Connect engagement and student-lifecycle information with the broader institutional record, giving teams greater context as students move through their relationship with the institution.
- **Help staff focus on the moments that matter most.** Apply AI to repetitive and time-intensive work so institutional teams can devote more attention to conversations and decisions where human expertise matters.


This approach reflects a shared vision in which technology and AI strengthen the work of institutional teams rather than replacing the people at the center of the student experience.


“We chose Element451, Student First, and Blackbaud because each one is the strongest system for its part of our campus,” said Mike Clark, Director of Business Process and Automation at Colby-Sawyer College. “The Connected Campus is what ties them together. Bringing these solutions into one connected model will let our teams spend less time moving information between offices and more time with students.”


**See the Connected Campus at HESS**


Blackbaud, Element451, Student First and Doctums will come together at the Higher Education Systems & Services (HESS) Consortium National Conference, Nov. 16–18 in Louisville, Kentucky. The partners will host a Connected Campus group workshop on Wednesday, Nov. 18, giving higher education leaders an opportunity to learn more about the ecosystem and its approach to connecting technology across campus.
